title: Route checks by job kind, skipping fmt/clippy only for prose-only change
summary: Build ci-routing.md section 10 item 5: a routing function in athena-core that maps the plan's class_of_work to the checks and their source (reused CI result via item 4 `resolve`, or local), following the 3.2 table. The 'as today' skip stays path-based (`skip_when_only`), so a job of any kind that changes Rust, Cargo.toml or Cargo.lock still runs fmt and clippy. The audience is the Athena maintainer and ci-routing.md reviewers.

defaults_applied.how: All code and tests are Rust.
Per-case routing tests; cargo test and clippy pass.
Behavior criteria name the cargo commands the verifier runs.
Criteria check routing outcomes per kind, including the Rust-changing docs job.
The skip rule stays path-based so a mislabelled kind cannot weaken checks.
One routing function with minimal config change.
The doc update states what is not measured.
The rule is enforced by tests, including a loaded-athena.toml test.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Section 3.2 says docs/design 'fmt and clippy skipped as today'; today's rule is path-based `skip_when_only` (docs/ and *.md), and section 6.1 says that rule is unchanged and verification is not weakened. Job kind never skips fmt or clippy by itself.
Study, config, tests and code jobs never get fmt/clippy skipped by kind. A study job gets the same gates as a change; any prose-only skip comes only from the path rule.
The `test` check always runs for every kind, because the policy tests read prose.
A build job adds the workflow's own run and never reuses a prior CI result.
A missing or unrecognised kind routes like config (fmt, clippy, test, none skipped), per section 7.
CI result reuse goes through item 4 `resolve` with the candidate SHA. A result for another SHA is ignored and the check runs locally. A red CI result fails and does not rerun locally.

The kind-specific data is only the reuse/source decision and the build extra. The skip decision stays on the existing `skip_when_only` fields, so athena.toml and the schema in athena-data/config.rs need little or no change. If a field is added, the schema, athena.toml and the capability crates' field copies change together.
No speedup is claimed or measured.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run `cargo test -p athena-core routing`: a docs-kind job whose changed paths are only markdown or under docs/ skips fmt and clippy and still runs test.

Run `cargo test -p athena-core routing`: for each of docs, design and study, a job that changes a .rs file runs fmt and clippy (one named test per kind). The same holds when only Cargo.toml or Cargo.lock changes.

Run `cargo test -p athena-core routing`: a code job and a tests job run fmt, clippy and test with none skipped. A config job never has any check skipped. A build job adds the workflow's own run and never reuses a prior result.
Run `cargo test -p athena-core routing`: a missing or unrecognised kind routes as config (fmt, clippy, test, none skipped).

Run `cargo test -p athena-core`: the routed path calls `resolve` with the candidate SHA. A CI result for another SHA is ignored and the check falls back to a local run. A red CI result fails the check and does not rerun locally.

Run `cargo test` including a test that loads the committed athena.toml with the schema in the tree: athena.toml parses, and representative jobs of each kind route as 3.2 says with the committed config.
Run `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`: both pass, and `cargo test` passes in full.

The routing function is called from the job run path (run.rs) to select the checks by the plan's kind, so a reader can find the call site. Skipping still uses the path rule, and no code path skips fmt or clippy by kind alone.

docs/design/ci-routing.md section 10 item 5 states what was built and what is not done, and does not claim a measured speedup. Its wording keeps 'skipped as today' as the path rule. CHANGELOG.md has an entry.
If the config schema or athena.toml changed, the change is limited to routing, is listed in the diff, and every crate that copies the field compiles.

out_of_scope: Measuring CI speedup or cache hit rates
Changing the CI workflow file or the build job (other items of section 10)
Changing the existing path-based skip_when_only rule for prose-only changes
departures: Cost is a little above the reference: the change touches many files and this is a retry after a rejection, so the verifier will check the skip rule closely.
